DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 06 s. 2021 27 January 2021 DIR. JOSEPHINE CABRIDO-LEYSA Regional Director, Region XII Prime Regional Government Center Carpenter Hill, Koronadal City Dear RD Leysa: This has reference to your letter dated 22 December 2020 relative to the letter from Provincial Director Ali B. Abdullah, DILG-Cotabato, regarding the legal effects of the transfer of the sixty-three (63) barangays of Cotabato Province to the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM vis-a-vis the incumbent member/s of the Liga ng mga Barangay therein. Specifically, PD Abdullah posed the following queries: 1. Whether or not the incumbent President of the Provincial Liga ng mga Barangay of Cotabato, Hon. Dulia D. Sultan, may continue to serve as Ex-Officio Provincial Board Member in the Province of Cotabato and the same time as the Regional Liga President after December 15, 2020 considering that her barangay was already transferred under the jurisdiction of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM); and 2. Whether or not the turnover of 63 barangays of North Cotabato to BARMM by virtue of Republic Act No. 11054 will give rise to a permanent vacancy in the position of Provincial Liga ng mga Barangay President in the event that the barangay of the current holder of the said position where he/she represents is part of the territorial transition. It appears that Cotabato City residents and those in the 63 villages of North Cotabato voted to become part of the BARMM through a plebiscite in January 20191. On 15 December 2020, they were turned over 1 https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1372111/cotabato-city-63-cotabato-province-villages-now-officially-part-of- barmm.

to the supervision of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM). On these circumstances arose the aforesaid queries from Provincial Director Abdullah. We shall answer both queries in one (1) discussion since they are interrelated. Section 39 of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 reads: SECTION 39. Qualifications. - (a) An elective local official must be a citizen of the Philippines; a registered voter in the Barangay, municipality, city, or province or, in the case of a member of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Sangguniang Panlungsod, or Sanggunian bayan, the district where he intends to be elected; a resident therein for at least one (1) year immediately preceding the day of the election; and able to read and write Filipino or any other local language or dialect. Under the law and jurisprudence, the above-enumerated qualifications of elective local officials are continuing, meaning, they should be possessed thereof from the time of election, except citizenship which may be possessed on the day of assumption, and until the expiration of the term of office. Any loss of qualifications obtaining prior to the expiration of the term of office could be a ground to assail the aforesaid official's incumbency in the office. The barangay where Hon. Dulia D. Sultan was elected as Punong Barangay was previously part of the Province of Cotabato. It was by virtue of her being the Punong Barangay therein that she was elected as President of the Provincial Liga ng mga Barangay of Cotabato. Then came RA 11054 or the "Organic Law for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao". It was by virtue of said law that the barangay where Hon. Sultan was elected as Punong Barangay was among those transferred under the jurisdiction of the BARMM. With such transfer of jurisdiction to BARMM, her qualification (i.e. as registered voter in the Barangay where he was elected) as Punong Barangay was lost and accordingly, her being President of the Provincial Liga ng mga Barangay of Cotabato can be validly argued to have ceased, thus paving the way for a permanent vacancy to said positions. As to who will discharge the legislative and executive powers in the BARMM, Section 3, in relation to Section 1, Article XVI of RA 11054 is instructive, thus:

Section 3. Powers and Authorities. Legislative and executive powers in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region during transition shall be vested in the Bangsamoro Transition Authority. During the transition period, executive authority shall be exercised by the interim Chief Minister who shall be appointed by the President as such, while legislative authority shall be exercised by the Bangsamoro Transition Authority. All powers and functions of the Bangsamoro Government as provided in this Organic Law is vested in the Bangsamoro Transition Authority during the transition period. For the purposes of mechanism for intergovernmental relations with the National Government and local government units in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region, The Bangsamoro Transition Authority shall be deemed as the Bangsamoro Government for the duration of the transition period Section 1. Transition Period - The transition period for the establishment of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region shall commence upon the ratification of this Organic Law. This Organic Law shall be deemed ratified when approved by a majority of the votes cast in a plebiscite as proclaimed by the Commission on Elections or its duly authorized officers. The transition period shall end upon the dissolution of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority as provided in this Organic Law. The transition period shall be without prejudice to the initiation or continuation of other measures that may be required by post-conflict transition and normalization even beyond the term of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority xxxx We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. By the Authority of the Secre ary: TIN B. DINO retary for Barangay Affairs n IS/ 17
